architecture_snapshot.wp206_problem: same-inode SQLite data/schema revision fencing without database-wide false positives

source_findings.finding: data_version changes on a connection when another connection commits to the database; same-connection commits do not change it; values are connection-local and meaningful only when compared on the same connection over time.
source_findings.f2_implication: Useful as a coarse live-connection signal that some external database write happened, but too broad to identify WP206-owned-state drift and not suitable as a persistent restart epoch by itself.

source_findings.finding: update hooks are per connection and observe many row INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE events on that connection, with documented omissions including WITHOUT ROWID and some REPLACE/truncate cases.
source_findings.f2_implication: Not a cross-process persistent foreign-writer witness and therefore insufficient for stale-authority fencing.

source_findings.finding: Persistent triggers can execute automatically on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE for selected tables and can update a durable revision row in the same transaction.
source_findings.f2_implication: Supports a table-specific persistent monotonic owned-state mutation witness that unrelated UnifiedDB tables do not bump.

source_findings.finding: sessions monitor configured tables for changes made through the associated connection/session and produce changesets.
source_findings.f2_implication: Useful for changeset capture but not an all-connection persistent external-writer witness.

source_findings.finding: trigger execution can be disabled per connection through SQLITE_DBCONFIG_ENABLE_TRIGGER; defensive configuration restricts dangerous schema manipulation but does not turn in-database triggers into an unbypassable external authority.
source_findings.f2_implication: A trigger revision counter must be paired with trigger/schema identity verification and an authorized-writer contract; it is not a hostile arbitrary-writer security boundary by itself.

source_findings.source: SQLite official ON CONFLICT / REPLACE behavior documentation
source_findings.finding: REPLACE may delete conflicting rows before inserting/replacing; delete-trigger behavior has recursive-trigger nuances.
source_findings.f2_implication: Treat the owned revision as a monotonic 'relevant state mutated' witness, not an exact operation counter; tests must cover REPLACE semantics explicitly.

hypothesis: For cooperative authorized UnifiedDB writers, a narrow persistent owned-state revision row, transactionally incremented by triggers on only WP206-owned tables and paired with schema/trigger identity verification, can detect same-inode authority-relevant drift without rejecting unrelated legitimate database writes.
counterhypotheses: If arbitrary writers may disable triggers or rewrite schema, an in-database revision counter is bypassable and cannot be the sole authority witness.
If WP206-owned state spans dynamic/unbounded tables, maintaining a trigger set may be more fragile than a deterministic digest of a bounded owned-state projection.
If the active G6 design already has a narrower equivalent revision contract, adding another mechanism would be duplicate architecture.

recommended_pattern.name: OWNED_STATE_REVISION_FENCE
components: persistent revision record scoped to WP206-owned state
AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE triggers on only WP206-owned tables that monotonically advance the revision inside the writer transaction
schema/trigger identity fence over the expected owned-table/trigger definitions
optional PRAGMA data_version as a cheap coarse signal that prompts selective re-check, never as the final authority decision
fail_closed_rules: owned revision changed unexpectedly -> stale-authority/reopen path, subject to current WP206 contract
expected trigger/schema identity changed or is missing -> fail closed
data_version changed but owned revision/schema identity did not -> treat as unrelated database activity, not WP206 authority replacement
do not infer hostile-writer resistance from cooperative trigger semantics

rejected_as_primary_witness: PRAGMA user_version as an automatically maintained revision
evidence_boundary: SOURCE_READ_AND_ARCHITECTURAL_INFERENCE_ONLY. No WP206 code mutation, repository CI, target runtime, or whole-system credit is granted. Active WP206 generation ownership remains external to Trigger 6.
next_exact_action: Refresh F2 main and active WP206 G6 ownership; if no Trigger-6 mapping objective already exists, acquire E2_ARCHITECTURE_MAPPED and map the smallest owned-state revision witness onto the current persistent_agency_kernel/UnifiedDB boundary without mutating the active workpackage.
